<problem>
For $S\subseteq\mathbb N$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $R_S(n)=|\{(s_1,s_2,s_3)\in S^3:\ s_1\le s_2\le s_3,\ s_1+s_2+s_3=n\}|$. Recall that $S$ is a Sidon set if all sums $s+s'$ with $s\le s'$, $s,s'\in S$, are distinct. Does there exist a Sidon set $S\subseteq\mathbb N$ such that $R_S(n)\ge1$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and $R_S(n)=n^{o(1)}$ as $n\to\infty$? Equivalently, up to $n^{o(1)}$ factors, is there a Sidon asymptotic basis of order $3$ that is essentially thin, i.e. with $|S\cap[N]|=N^{1/3+o(1)}$ and no unusually large representation counts? As a stronger form, can one even have $R_S(n)\ll\log n$ for all large $n$?
</problem>

<solution>
Answer: Yes, in the strong form. There is a Sidon set $S\subseteq\mathbb N$ with $1\le R_S(n)\ll\log n$ for all sufficiently large $n$; hence $R_S(n)=n^{o(1)}$ and $|S\cap[N]|\ll (N\log N)^{1/3}=N^{1/3+o(1)}$.

1. Existence of a Sidon asymptotic basis of order 3. This is the Erdős–Sárközy–Sós problem (1994); Cilleruelo (2015) got order $3+\varepsilon$, and C. Pilatte (Compositio Math. 2024, "A solution to the Erdős–Sárközy–Sós problem on asymptotic Sidon bases of order 3") proved there is a Sidon set $S$ with $R_S(n)\ge1$ for all large $n$. The construction is probabilistic: $S$ is a random subset (independent inclusions, probabilities of size $\asymp m^{-2/3}(\log m)^{1/3}$ up to a structural factor) of an ambient set built from Bose–Chowla/Erdős–Turán-type Sidon sets, chosen so that the expected number $\mu_n$ of representations $a+b+c=n$ is $\asymp \log n$; Janson's inequality gives $\Pr(R(n)=0)\le n^{-2}$ and Borel–Cantelli gives $R(n)\ge 1$ for all large $n$, while the structure of the ambient set controls the additive quadruples so that the Sidon property can be achieved without destroying the basis property.

2. The bound $R_S(n)\ll\log n$. 
(a) Lemma (Sidon sets): let $D_S(n)$ be the maximal number of pairwise disjoint representations of $n$ as $s_1\le s_2\le s_3$. Every representation meets one of the $\le 3D_S(n)$ elements of a maximal disjoint family, and for fixed $s$ the representations containing $s$ correspond to pairs $s_2\le s_3$ with $s_2+s_3=n-s$, of which a Sidon set has at most one. Hence $R_S(n)\le 3D_S(n)$. Also $D$ is monotone under taking subsets.
(b) Erdős–Tetali tail bound: for a random set $\mathcal S$ with independent inclusions, disjoint representations are independent events, so $\Pr(D_{\mathcal S}(n)\ge k)\le \mu_n^k/k!\le (e\mu_n/k)^k$. With $\mu_n\ll\log n$ and $k=C\log n$ this is $\le n^{-2}$; Borel–Cantelli gives $D_{\mathcal S}(n)\ll\log n$ for all large $n$ a.s.
Since the final Sidon set $S$ is contained in the random set $\mathcal S$ whose expected representation counts are $O(\log n)$ (in the ambient set, two summands in prescribed Sidon pieces determine the third, so the count is bounded by products of piece sizes times inclusion probabilities, which is $O(\log n)$), we get $1\le R_S(n)\le 3D_S(n)\le 3D_{\mathcal S}(n)\ll\log n$ for all large $n$.

3. Consequences and sharpness. $\binom{|S\cap[N]|+2}{3}\le\sum_{n\le 3N}R_S(n)\ll N\log N$ gives $|S\cap[N]|\ll (N\log N)^{1/3}$, optimal up to the log since any order-3 basis has $|S\cap[N]|\gg N^{1/3}$ (and Sidon forces $\ll N^{1/2}$). The factor $\log n$ is the natural barrier: any probabilistic construction with $R(n)\ge1$ for all large $n$ needs $\mu_n\gtrsim\log n$, and a basis of order 3 with bounded representation function is open even without the Sidon condition.

Final answer: Yes — there exists a Sidon asymptotic basis of order 3 with $R_S(n)\ll\log n$ (hence $R_S(n)=n^{o(1)}$ and $|S\cap[N]|=N^{1/3+o(1)}$). The existence is Pilatte's theorem; the logarithmic bound on the representation function follows from the probabilistic construction via the lemma $R_S(n)\le 3D_S(n)$ for Sidon sets and the Erdős–Tetali disjoint-family tail bound.
</solution>
